raw.assessment: The incumbent supplies an assembled organizer, checks the order, and offers layout guidance. Repeated three-compartment orders took seven to nine minutes, so near-target workshop performance occurs under some conditions. Mixed batches contained every extreme delay, but layout complexity and switching are confounded. Missing/incorrect-part reports and short-partition questions indicate distinct fulfillment and comprehension concerns; their causes remain unestablished. A concrete limit on a simple dimensional explanation is D2-O5: widths overlap between first-attempt and retry parts. Width alone therefore does not separate those groups. Neither zero recorded damage claims nor the small unpacking session establishes pilot success.

openings.claim: Switching between order requirements may increase selection/checking time and component errors; order-specific temporary kits may reduce that burden.
openings.delta: Replace shared-bin selection during assembly with a counted tray of the exact ordered parts and exterior color, using reusable board dividers.
openings.prediction: For matched layouts, temporary kits reduce total preparation-through-packing time and discrepancies, especially after layout switches. Unchanged selection time with persistent insertion delays weakens this account.
openings.probe: Use five reusable sample sets in counterbalanced mixed and grouped sequences across both workers. Compare current selection with counted kits; time kit preparation, selection, insertion, checking and packing separately, and audit contents against each order. Treat repetitions as diagnostic, not independent pilot orders.
assumptions: Kit preparation is included in total labor.
Reusable supplies fit the initial budget; implementation must meet the recurring-cost cap and fixed date.

openings.claim: The generic three-layout diagram may leave the short partition's ordered position ambiguous; an order-specific diagram may improve unaided arrangement.
openings.delta: Show the selected arrangement with the short partition and its insertion orientation clearly identified.
openings.prediction: Correct first placement and fewer location questions support a comprehension benefit. Correct identification followed by repeated insertion failures instead indicates a remaining mechanical limitation.
openings.probe: Allocate ten remaining samples and ten participants between existing and revised diagrams, balancing layout complexity. Record first placement, insertion retries, unaided completion and elapsed time. This small comparison screens the hypothesis; verify the 90% threshold in the pilot.
assumptions: Diagram replacement fits cost and delivery limits.
Parts, footprint, capacity, removability, ordered compartment counts and exterior colors remain as specified.

raw.assessment: Two transferable relationships merit tests. Mixed-batch delays, reported component errors and short-partition confusion do not establish a common cause. Neither alternative establishes pilot success.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: adapt surgical instrument count trays into reusable, order-specific partition trays. Each required part occupies one outlined position before assembly; the order slip specifies compartment count and exterior color.
openings.delta: Map visible instrument completeness to visible kit completeness, replacing direct assembly from shared bins. Failed correspondence: similar board partitions can occupy incorrect outlines. Changed material assumptions: sample-derived length/profile outlines and one layer per position are necessary; current parts and removable joints remain.
openings.prediction: Selection/checking time and omission/substitution escapes decrease; insertion retries need not change.
openings.probe: Reuse six sample sets across balanced current-process and tray trials with both workers and mixed layouts. Separately time selection, insertion, checking and packing. Blind-check seeded missing/incorrect parts in nondelivery trials. Cost fabrication and upkeep.
assumptions: Trays fit the 500 initial and 0.40 recurring limits without delaying delivery.
A verified parts specification exists for every accepted layout and color.

openings.claim: Adapt computer bootstrapping: supply a starting configuration with the short partition seated, letting customers finish their exact ordered arrangement using its diagram.
openings.delta: Map a minimal working state enabling configuration to a physical orientation anchor. Failed correspondence: customers do not execute instructions deterministically; anchors may obstruct subsequent insertions. Changed material assumptions: partial assembly replaces full assembly, loose parts require retention, and the anchor stays removable.
openings.prediction: Workshop insertion time falls; helpful anchors reduce short-partition placement errors, whereas obstructive anchors increase reseating.
openings.probe: Use nine remaining sample sets and ten participants, balancing layout difficulty between current and anchored presentations. Record unaided completion, anchor removal, final contents and workshop packing time. Test loose-part retention and incremental cost.
assumptions: Every accepted layout permits an anchor without changing capacity, footprint, count or exterior color.
Retention and preparation satisfy both cost limits and the fixed deadline.
Small trials indicate direction; the 60-unit pilot must establish all stated thresholds.

openings.claim: Counted order trays may reduce switching burden and omissions/substitutions; use length/profile outlines, one layer per position, verified layout/color specifications.
openings.discriminator: Selection/checking and escapes improve; insertion retries may persist.
openings.probe: Counterbalance workers, layouts, mixed/grouped sequences and current/tray methods; time preparation through packing by stage; audit contents, blind-check seeded nondelivery errors, cost upkeep.
openings.uncertainty: Complexity confounds switching; similar parts defeat outlines; preparation may erase savings.

openings.claim: Order-specific diagrams may clarify short-partition position/orientation.
openings.discriminator: Better placement/fewer questions versus correct identification with mechanical retries.
openings.probe: Balance layouts across existing/revised diagrams; record placement, retries, unaided completion/time.
openings.uncertainty: Small screen only; overlapping widths cannot explain retry differences.

openings.claim: Partial assembly with a removable seated short partition may anchor orientation and save insertion labor.
openings.discriminator: Fewer placement errors versus obstructive reseating.
openings.fit: Uncertain: anchor compatibility across layouts and loose-part retention.
openings.probe: Compare current/anchored presentations by layout; record completion, anchor removal, contents, packing time; test retention/cost.
openings.uncertainty: Customer variation; zero damage claims do not establish retention.

post_distill.decision: Screen sequentially within 15 samples/ten participants; repetitions remain diagnostic. Preserve 30x20 cm, assortment, removability, accepted counts/colors, deadline; costs <=500 initial/0.40 recurring. Require 60-order pilot: >=98% complete, median total workshop time <=8 minutes, >=90% unaided arrangement. Success unestablished.
